### Off to Egypt
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/egypt
Passage: Genesis 37:28
Points:
- The brothers' callous hearts are revealed when they sit down to eat immediately after casting Joseph into a pit.
- Judah proposes selling Joseph into slavery as a way to dispose of him while making a financial profit.
- Joseph is sold for twenty shekels of silver, a substantial sum in the ancient shepherd economy.
- Although the brothers sought to destroy Joseph's dreams, God used their evil deeds to bring those dreams to pass.
- Joseph's undeserved mistreatment foreshadows Jesus Christ, who endured innocent suffering to redeem His people.

### A Sin Concealed
Author: R.C. Sproul
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/a-sin-concealed
Passage: Genesis 37:12-30
Points:
- Jacob sent Joseph on a long, perilous journey to check on his brothers and the flocks.
- Harboring deep-seated jealousy, the brothers plotted to kill Joseph as soon as they saw him approaching in the distance.
- Reuben intervened to prevent outright murder, suggesting they cast Joseph into a dry pit so he could rescue him later.
- The brothers demonstrated extreme hardness of heart by eating a meal while their brother languished in the pit.
- Judah convinced them to sell Joseph to traveling Midianite and Ishmaelite traders for twenty pieces of silver.
- Joseph's betrayal and sale for silver prefigures Jesus Christ being betrayed by His disciple for thirty pieces of silver.

### Bible Pathway - Jan. 13, 2011
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-jan-13-2011-11644032.html
Passage: Genesis 37:23-28
Points:
- Joseph showed upright spiritual integrity even when it provoked the hostility of his brothers.
- Overcome by envy and resentment, the brothers stripped Joseph of his distinctive robe and threw him into an empty pit.
- Rather than leaving him to die, they sold him into slavery to passing Ishmaelite traders.
- God was with Joseph through his betrayal and used his suffering in Egypt to preserve the covenant lineage.
- Joseph's rejection, suffering, and eventual exaltation serve as a type of Jesus Christ.
